A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same topic-model unlearning work. The text, equations, algorithms, table and complete appendices are readable and matchable; v3 adds Appendix C.3.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical guarantees and proofs, including in its appendices. Table 1 gives asymptotic runtime bounds, not original empirical measurements.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical throughout. Its additional appendix analyzes approximate optimization without reporting experiments, simulations or original data analyses.

M1.justification: Definition 2 and Appendix C.3 extend downstream unlearning to tau-optimal heads, replacing the exact-head requirement for this variant and adjusting Gaussian noise for optimization error. The base algorithm and Newton-step/pseudoinverse structure are retained.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets. Topic modeling and downstream classification remain theoretical settings; C.3 adds no evaluated task or population.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same analytical comparison between retraining and unlearning. Neither version reports evaluated empirical baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols or evaluation settings. The new optimization tolerance concerns the theoretical formulation, not a revised or additional experiment.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, empirical robustness tests, error analyses or case studies. Appendix C.3 is a theoretical proof extension.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty estimates or significance tests. Their probabilistic guarantees concern theoretical unlearning and concentration.

E6.justification: The asymptotic runtime entries in Table 1 are unchanged, and neither version reports empirical outcomes. The added inexact-minimizer guarantees are theoretical changes assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v3 generalizes Definition 2 and adds Appendix C.3 with Definition 9, Assumption 8, Lemmas 33–38 and Propositions 8–9. These extend stability, Newton-error, sensitivity and utility arguments to inexact heads under tau = O(1/r), culminating in a deletion-capacity guarantee. This substantively broadens the theory beyond v1's exact-minimizer treatment.

C1.justification: The abstract, results overview and conclusion retain the same main contributions: efficient provable unlearning, task-dependent deletion-capacity advantages, and downstream unlearning without modifying the base model.

C2.justification: Section 5 now explicitly distinguishes exact optimization used for exposition from the more realistic inexact regime. Footnote 1 clarifies that the asymptotic results extend to other constant document lengths. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: For the inexact-head variant, C.3 specifies the optimality tolerance, its required scaling and a tau-dependent Gaussian-noise calibration in Lemma 35. These supplement v1's exact-head specifications; no code, hardware or experimental implementation information is added.

R1.justification: Section 6 and the reference list retain the same works and research positioning. The novelty claims relative to prior unlearning research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The existing narrative and section order are largely retained. Local edits introduce tau-head-tuning terminology, explanatory pointers and small wording corrections; v3 also adds equal-contribution attribution, updates the publication header and appends C.3.

P2.justification: v3 removes displayed-equation numbering and makes limited equation and page reflow adjustments. Table 1 and the six algorithm displays retain their structure and placement; no figures are added.

improvement.justification: v1's downstream analysis assumes exactly optimized heads. v3 accounts explicitly for finite optimization error and its effect on noise and utility, improving practical relevance and theoretical completeness. The gain is bounded: it requires tau = O(1/r), retains the existing main guarantees, and only indicates how to extend the new argument to general q.
